claims.statement: Deluge shares a direct authenticated torrent-state RPC helper between startup/liveness probes and cached metrics while retaining the existing VPN and Web readiness gates and local-config/QNAP-download storage layout.
Traefik is a stateless Argo CD ingress application dependent on cert-manager, Istio and Tailscale; the staged Tailscale operator configuration enables its authenticated Kubernetes API proxy.

Image Updater has staged Helm/Kustomize source configured with zero replicas but no root Terragrunt Application registration; its runbook records the Application and Deployment as absent on 2026-10-10.
cert-manager's registered Application uses chart v1.20.3 and its versioned digest-pinned values, while rollback to v1.19.2 restores matching values from the documented pre-upgrade Git revision.

Phase2a routes internal Octelium API and Harbor DNS through Traefik, advertises n8n's Funnel webhook URL and declares Cordium bootstrap peers, while retaining runtime legacy routes and credentials until staged acceptance.

Fleet's declared route stays private through Tailscale and Traefik with setup denied, while PolicyBot's fixed GitHub App callback migration requires Funnel preflight and a fresh signed delivery before legacy route retirement.
The retained connector has temporary access only to Traefik port8443 by exact ambient principal and intended namespace-plus-pod selector, until connector retirement after acceptance.

Mastodon follows main through its shared Application stack, depends on SSM, External Secrets, cert-manager, Istio, public connector and platform storage, and routes its instance hostname to web port 3000 and streaming port 4000 while preserving the private apex portal.

Mastodon retains local PostgreSQL and AOF Redis volumes on zimaboard-1, NAS media and checked nightly database backups with 14-day retention; shared NAS storage is not independent disaster recovery and recovery must preserve stable application keys.

Mastodon orders schema preparation before idempotent owner bootstrap and Deployments, refuses SMTP placeholders, and separates declared registration from public DNS publication, which requires both Applications healthy at the reviewed revision.

Langfuse web is a stateless Acer-pinned Pod with a 1280 MiB request and unchanged 2 GiB limit, freeing its former 2 GiB reservation on Cordium-eligible zimaboard-1; worker and CPU budgets are unchanged.

The root Terragrunt stack declares a platform image-policy Argo CD Application using Warn and Audit admission, with no storage or credentials; live audit evidence and any Deny promotion require separate acceptance.
The Cordium Actions runner pool remains disabled with no controller Deployment or published runner image; hosted selectors remain until isolation, private pull, canary, and cleanup acceptance pass.

Fleet's Apple baseline operator remains host-scoped and retains Fleet as Mac MDM. Fleet-only Company Portal/Platform SSO is retired; console SAML is separate from owner conversion, which is currently blocked by the federated target domain.
The staged native Harbor Chainguard receipt covers private Python and curl imports but does not publish those images or migrate consumers; protected receipt and provenance gates remain prerequisites.

Tailnet DNS is a separate stateless Argo CD resolver in its own namespace, backed by CoreDNS and k8s_gateway, exposed through a distinct signed Tailscale DNS proxy; its pinned Harbor image must be published before rollout.

The Renovate Application declares an unsuspended hourly UTC full dry-run CronJob with a retained 20 Gi NFS cache, dedicated no-token ServiceAccount, and Harbor alias to a registry-only Traefik listener. Protected App-key transfer and temporary writer-grant retirement are complete; the legacy GitHub Action remains the writer while eligible Harbor discovery, T024/T042 cache-fault and NAS-capacity recovery, full dry-run parity, and reviewed cutover remain open.

Legacy OpenClaw's gateway and backup writer are stopped by GitOps; local and NAS state and four PVC/PV identities remain. The protected off-NAS archive publication passed, while an independent restore verification is running. Enterprise activation remains disabled, and no canary node is admissible at current capacity.

The Enterprise platform branch registers NetworkPolicy, canary, cleanup and Envoy Gateway Argo Applications with automatic sync disabled; kube-router selects no node, canary fixtures stay empty before admission, and no private route or firewall enforcement is accepted from registration alone.

LiteLLM's reviewed consumer source pins the Linux amd64 child of a repeated-descriptor OCI index that Harbor 2.15.2 rejects. Protected scoped run 39210811031 published that exact child before the consumer source changed; all four observed nodes were amd64 on October 19, and full-catalog publication remains pending.

OpenClaw Enterprise's source-declared, unsynced foundation prepares restricted system and tenant namespaces, RoleBindings, eight retained SSM projections, ingress denial, PostgreSQL certificates, and a dormant PostgreSQL 18.6 StatefulSet with 10Gi local claim template; no database, PVC, route or Installation workload is running from this source.

Separate staged Octelium and Traefik declarations add an authenticated OpenClaw Enterprise console and exact opaque-Agent private API hosts while the old OpenClaw URL still targets the suspended legacy Service; no Enterprise access has passed live acceptance.

The dormant OpenClaw Enterprise stock-chart candidate declares reviewed Installation startup bytes, immutable Secret contract, Helm values and lifecycle hooks; separate auto-sync-disabled Terragrunt Applications declare foundation and chart registration but have not been applied or synced, and placement and database/storage gates prevent activation.

Kiali's source-owned ingress policy replaces the operator-generated policy with an equivalent complete TCP 20001/9090 spec. The read-only recheck found the operator policy absent and source policy present; Octelium and Prometheus traffic, broad-source review, and isolated canary enforcement remain open.
Nine repository-owned DNS egress policies select CoreDNS Pods on TCP and UDP port 53; offline source checks pass while isolated-canary traffic qualification remains open.

The source-only T018 pass narrows declared Cloudflared egress to labeled Istio and Octelium dataplane Pods, Harbor metrics ingress to Prometheus Pods, and Harbor nginx and Mastodon ingress to labeled gateway Pods; Harbor nginx retains Traefik and bootstrap peers, and Mastodon adds ambient HBONE TCP/15008. Flannel does not yet enforce these NetworkPolicies, so endpoint and traffic behavior require isolated-canary verification.

Renovate T022 is complete: scheduled 19:00 and 20:00 Pods hit the same public canary cache key, and after protected v0.0.2 publication the 21:00 scheduled run refreshed the record and selected a new canary branch proposal.

Renovate T045 is complete: retained 17:00 repository-tagged lookup failures and alerts recovered in the 18:00 Job; the 03:00 missed-slot drill fired RenovateHourlyCycleMissing, and the restored 04:00 scheduled Job succeeded after alert clearance.

The 2026-10-20 13:07–13:15 UTC post-shutdown recheck leaves Enterprise placement blocked: the best worker has about 3,398 MiB unreserved versus a 4,096 MiB initial steady request and 9.74 GB root-filesystem space free; all workers have less than 10.74 GB for a new 10 GiB local claim under the existing /var/lib pattern, acer lacks the 2,304 MiB database-plus-gateway minimum, and unrelated Pods prevent NoSchedule taint isolation.

Read-only expected-spec fixtures source-bind three Cordium policies at pinned v0.12.7, four Octelium Genesis policies at pinned v0.35.0, and ten Octelium Enterprise generated policies; all 17 complete specs are bound, while pinned generator-binary renders and live enforcement remain unverified.

Pinned Cordium ws-main and Octelium svc-upstream constructors hardcode public IPv4 and IPv6 all-port egress without a configuration input; additive NetworkPolicies cannot narrow them. Reviewed upstream patches or forks, rebuilt pinned images, actual generator renders, and isolated canary traffic qualification remain required before enforcement.

The protected Enterprise workflow invokes a pinned full-sync helper, but the committed unselected installation phase blocks Kubernetes sync. Reconcile, stop, and verification now route through a source-bound exact-main one-shot Job dispatcher, yet the disabled operator gate prevents Job creation; restore and acceptance remain separately blocked. Offline fixtures check source, identity, and dependency ordering.

An offline-tested Enterprise Installation binder can attest and bind the reviewed startup Secret. A fixed protected binding lane is declared, but hosted-runner delivery of its owner-controlled 0600 bootstrap key and any live binding receipt remain absent.

The source-only Enterprise reconciler journals one logical Namespace, Configuration and stopped Embedded Agent; its offline-tested active path guards a native-origin generation-2 update and second revision while preserving uncertain stop intent. A one-shot operator Job path and clean-source operator image recipe are staged but no Job or Agent is live; activation is disabled, the distinct OpenRouter key is absent, and PV placement, signed operator digest and bootstrap file proof remain pending.

The dormant network-policy cleanup Application follows reviewed fixture and firewall removal commits. Live fixture resources block ownership stages, and private owner approval of a versioned snapshot gates rule deletion. Capture through release reject canary-node Pods outside reviewed system and cleanup Pod identities while cleanup runs; after cleanup Pod deletion, release rechecks only reviewed system Pods before taint removal. Changed system Pod UID after firewall removal requires separately reviewed recovery.

Pod inventory checks and firewall deletion are not atomic, so a Pod tolerating the isolation taint could arrive during deletion; live activation remains blocked until isolated placement excludes that arrival or a reviewed repository-owned isolation path is added.

The Enterprise operator bundle is unregistered source that declares a retained 1Gi local journal claim, read-only proof RBAC, and private-network intent; the absent static PV and safe node placement prevent live admission.

The 2026-10-23 read-only checks leave Enterprise activation blocked: only acer has local disk for the distinct claims, its 503 MiB database-plus-gateway shortfall is only the declared floor, and co-locating the 4,096 MiB initial planning reservation would exceed its unreserved requests by about 2,295 MiB before transients. The separate agent placement lacks measured headroom; relocating unrelated workloads has not admitted an isolated canary.
The dormant Enterprise backup candidate requires exactly one stopped-writer marker with a nonempty claim UID, but there is no scheduled backup, live UID proof, or sustained writer fence.
The active Istio Application remains on 1.27.3 with automated self-heal, while the 1.28.10 chart candidate is disabled and outside the Argo source and Kustomize output.

The Istio runbook records a December 2026 retirement risk for the active GCS chart source and requires later AppProject, active source, and chart mirror migration even if the version upgrade stays held.

Enterprise stop and stopped verification require both the runtime response and an independent unfiltered raw PodList in the dedicated openclaw-agents tenant Namespace; it must have a resource version, no continuation page, and no Pods. Tenant RBAC grants pods/list, while uncertain or remaining Pods block stop completion.
